title: Patch: a private lobby left open across an update moves onto the new card patch, instead of refusing every Start as "update required"

**Issue #4072 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4072: Patch: a private lobby left open across an update moves onto the new card patch, instead of refusing every Start as "update required"
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Friends gather in a private lobby, pick their decks and press Ready. If JackiOh updates to a new card patch while they wait (the live site updates once a day, and nearly every update carries a new patch), that lobby can never start: every press of Start, and every friend who tries to join it, is answered "update required". Reloading does not help, because it is the lobby, not the player's browser, that remembers the old cards. The only way out today is for the host to close it and gather everyone again under a new code, four people at once for a 2v2.

Once this is built, a lobby that has not started moves onto the new patch the first time anyone opens or touches it after the update. Everyone's deck pick and Ready are taken off, since each deck was checked against the old cards. Each member's screen shows them choosing again, and once they pick and ready up the host's Start works.

## Why

- A lobby records the catalog version only when it is made: `crates/server/src/lobby/mod.rs:524` (`catalog_version: app.catalog.version.clone()` in `create`). Every later write copies the version it read (`lobby/store.rs:276`, `catalog_version = $9::text`, bound from `next.catalog_version` at `:292`), and nothing in `lobby/` ever sets it again.
- `enter` (`lobby/mod.rs:625-626`) and `start` (`lobby/mod.rs:949-950`) both refuse when it is not the running catalog: `if lobby.catalog_version != app.catalog.version { return Err(ApiError::new(ApiErrorCode::UpdateRequired, "update required")); }`. Picking again does not help. `pick` (`:729-758`) freezes the new deck under the running catalog but leaves the lobby's version where it was.
- The lobby screen shows the server's message as it comes (`apps/web/src/net/errors.ts:6`, `messageOf`). So a player on the current build is told "update required", and a reload reads the same lobby again.
- The catalog version is the newest shipped patch's (`crates/cards/build.rs`, the last entry of `crates/cards/patches/patches.json`). Fifteen patches shipped from 2026-11-13 to 2026-11-16 (v0.6.1 to v0.6.5c), and production is promoted once a day, staging every two hours (`docs/deploy-cloudflare.md:14`). So most deploys change it.
- R3730000 keeps lobbies in Postgres so that a deploy does not lose them ("Rejected: … a lobby kept in the server's memory, which a deploy would lose"). Yet any deploy that ships a patch makes every unstarted lobby unusable until its TTL runs out (`ttl_of`, `lobby/mod.rs:83-88`: 15 minutes for 1v1, 10 for co-op and 2v2). Meanwhile a friend's row still offers Join to it (R3732001, `lobbies_open_of_hosts`), and that Join is refused the same way.
- R3730002 is right that Start checks the running catalog again, since a frozen pick was checked under the old one (§9.4, `spec/09-architecture.md:53`: a stale catalog version is rejected "at every door into a match"). But no ruling says how an open lobby reaches the new catalog, and nothing in the code does it. `crates/server/tests/api/lobbies.rs` has no test of a lobby under an older catalog. The only such test, the `stale_catalog` module of `tests/api/duos_rooms.rs`, covers a co-op room's join refusing one; a room is one person's code and cheap to remake, but a lobby is a group gathered.

## Proposal

1. Make the move in `lobby/mod.rs`'s `load`, beside the write that already drops a blocked guest as the lobby is read (R1689000's reading, `:303-318`). When the lobby has not started and its `catalog_version` is not `app.catalog.version`:
   - Write it through `write` (a compare-and-set on its revision, the TTL run from now, every member told by a `lobby` frame over `/ws/social`).
   - Set `catalog_version` to the running one, remove every seat's pick and turn every Ready off. Seats, teams and settings stay.
   - Log it as `lobby.catalog_moved` with both versions.
   - If the compare-and-set loses because another member's read moved it first, read once more rather than answering `409 changed`.
2. Keep the checks in `enter` and `start`. They then catch only a deploy that lands between a read and its write.
3. Add a new ruling in the issue's block, with a test named after it. It amends R3730002, and R3730003's list of what takes picks and Readies off: an unstarted lobby follows the running catalog, and a started one is left alone, since its game already pinned its catalog (R767000). Hearthstone keeps no lobby across a patch, so nothing there decides this.
4. Alternatives the ruling should record as rejected:
   - Re-freezing each member's saved deck behind their back: they may have edited it since they picked, so their Ready would agree to a deck they never chose, and a random pick was dealt from the old card pools.
   - Keeping the picks whose cards still pass the deck checks: the same objection applies to random decks, and it is more code for a once-a-day case.
   - Closing the lobby when the catalog changes: in effect what happens today, and the group has to gather again.

No client change is needed. The lobby screen already reads the lobby again on its `lobby` frame (`apps/web/src/lobby/LobbyScreen.tsx:145`), and a seat with no pick is shown as choosing (`lobby/mod.rs:379`).

## Where it lands

- `crates/server/src/lobby/mod.rs`: `load`, and the module header's note on what a read may write.
- `crates/server/tests/api/lobbies.rs`: the new tests. Also `crates/server/tests/actor/social_live.rs`, if the members' frame is checked there.
- `spec/rulings/R<next free in the issue's block>.md`, with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`, and an "Amended by" line on R3730002 and R3730003.
- §9.4's Private lobbies line, `spec/09-architecture.md:69` ("checks the catalog and both seats again").

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Best of 1: a test makes the lobby, seats a guest and has both members pick and ready. It then sets the stored lobby's `catalog_version` to an older string through the store (`lobbies_get`, then `lobbies_update`), as the `stale_catalog` test in `duos_rooms.rs` fakes a room made before a deploy. The next read shows both seats choosing and nobody ready. After both pick and ready again, the host's Start answers 200 with a match id. Today it answers 409 `update_required` however often they pick again.
- [ ] The same holds for a co-op lobby and for a 2v2 lobby, whose four seats and teams are kept.
- [ ] A friend entering a lobby left under an older catalog takes the empty seat (200), not 409 `update_required`.
- [ ] Every member is told by a `lobby` frame when the lobby moves.
- [ ] A started lobby under an older catalog is not rewritten.
- [ ] When two members' reads race to move it, both get the lobby (no `409 changed`), and it moves once.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check` passes with the ruling note, its pending paragraph and its tests.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` are green.

## Size and risks

Small to medium (`difficulty:medium`): about 30 to 50 lines in `lobby/mod.rs`, four to six server tests and one ruling note. It is server only: no migration, no change to what the lobby read sends, no client change.

Risks:
- A read that writes is how `load` already drops a blocked guest, so the pattern is the module's own. The builder must keep the move safe when several reads race: the compare-and-set and one re-read.
- After an update, each member presses pick and Ready again. That is the price of never starting a game on a deck the running catalog has not checked.
```
